To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CSF biomarker profile of BD patients is different from that of healthy individuals.

the CSF levels of 5-HIAA, HVA, and DOPAC, and the ratio of HVA/5-HIAA were lower in patients with bipolar disorder compared to healthy controls, and these biomarkers were associated with clinical variables.

the use of the 5-HTTLPR and BDNF polymorphisms in the diagnosis of bipolar disorder has not been validated, that the use of these polymorphisms as predictors of treatment response has not been validated. 1,2,3.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of biomarkers that may be used to predict response to treatment in patients with bipolar disorder.
the identification of biomarkers that can be used in the early diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease and in the evaluation of the efficacy of drugs in the treatment of this disease.
the identification of biomarkers in CSF that may help in the diagnosis of BD and in the assessment of treatment response in patients with BD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a paucity of evidence for the use of CSF biomarkers in bipolar disorder.
there is no evidence that CSF levels of BDNF are significantly different in patients with BD than in healthy controls.
, at present, there is not sufficient evidence to recommend routine use of any of the available biomarkers to diagnose or monitor bipolar disorder.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most promising CSF biomarkers for bipolar disorder are the neurofilament light chain, the glutamate, the kynurenine pathway, the neurosteroids and the neuroinflammation biomarkers.
we have identified several biomarkers in cerebro-spinal fluid of bipolar patients versus healthy controls.
we found a number of biomarker candidates that could be used for the diagnosis of bipolar disorder.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the brain's immune system, or glia, is activated in bipolar disorder and this activation is associated with the severity of the illness.
there is a lot of evidence for the involvement of the glutamate system in bipolar disorder.
we have a new tool for identifying patients with bipolar disorder, a condition that is difficult to diagnose.
